effective_design.contrast: wrapper selects a role/argument interpretation versus wrapper is orthographic notation around one invariant meaning
effective_design.countermodel: Renderer stripping may discard semantically decisive material, or the shared payload may be a chance formal collision with no role relation.
effective_design.falsifier: Independent role coding finds no reproducible wrapper-conditioned slot change across paired payloads, while payload-only and wrapper models tie.
effective_design.mechanism: outer-wrapper role operator over stable payload
effective_design.prediction: Across held paired forms, wrapper changes should predict a fixed change in edge/node or state/figure argument slot while the inner payload remains stable; unwrapped payload-only matching should not predict the role.
effective_design.principal_risk: The source explicitly reports proximity-only ownership and no semantic role binding.
effective_design.related: Near GDT198 and IDEA000035/039, but narrows the proposition to an explicit wrapper-to-role operation rather than payload reuse, instrument/endpoint, or component identity.

source_evidence.quote:
Two of the three all-reading-stable figure-associated labels share the same
renderer-stripped HPR2 payload as one of the six tube-state labels:

| figure label | tube label | shared payload | surface change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dotedy` (`f77r.8`) | `otedy` (`f77r.3`) | `e|NONE|DY1|B30` | add outer `d` wrapper |
| `otchdy` (`f77r.49`) | `dchdy` (`f77r.6`) | `ch|NONE|DY1|B30` | `d` wrapper versus `OT` frame |

The southwest figure label supplies a weaker third resemblance: ZL3b writes
`otolaiin | o`, while IT2a/RF1b join `otolaiino`; its initial `otol` equals the
fourth tube label, but the reading-dependent boundary prevents an exact
payload comparison.

This is a coherent local compiler pattern: opaque payload can remain stable
while its left rendering changes with visual label class.  It is not strong
enough to identify a role.  Across all 84 assignments of three figure roles to
the nine stable labels, 20 achieve at least the observed two cross-class
matches (**p=0.238095**).  Neither matched pair shares a complete surface or
full HPR2 tuple, and all human ownership is proximity-only.

effective_design.unit: paired complete forms sharing renderer-stripped payload but differing in outer frame

findings.detail: Pair1 is otedy→dotedy (prepend d), tube-associated→figure-associated. Pair2 is otchdy→dchdy (replace initial ot with d), figure-associated→tube-associated. These are not the same surface rewrite, and d occurs on opposite class sides. They do not establish one fixed d-to-figure or d-to-tube operator. They also do not refute a context-dependent operator, toggle, or distinct operator realization: none is specified in the effective design.

findings.issue: Projected identity is not a fixed raw payload unit
findings.detail: The equal objects are renderer-stripped HPR2 tuples e|NONE|DY1|B30 and ch|NONE|DY1|B30. The primary explicitly says neither complete surface nor full HPR2 tuple matches. A test must state the transformation and which raw content is preserved before treating projection equality as semantic argument identity.

Prediction offers edge/node or state/figure argument slot without choosing one. Physical label association could support a purely structural contrast without known translations, but figure versus tube association is not already a directed argument relation. Proximity-only ownership is a limit on the given ownership inference, not a blanket ban on structural tests.

findings.issue: Capacity for stated transfer not supplied
findings.detail: Both exact pairs are exposed on f77r; the weaker third is segmentation-dependent. No held paired forms, repeated instance of the same frozen rewrite, or separate held physical folio is identified. The two pairs cannot simultaneously define an operator and serve as untouched confirmation.

Orthographic notation around invariant meaning can correlate with local visual class; payload-only can predict class if payload frequencies differ. A generic operator does not guarantee classifier separation. A tied or underpowered classifier cannot refute all wrapper operators.

predecessor_boundary: GDT198 already counts two cross-class projected-payload matches, with20/84 assignments as good or better. Repeating that count is not a new directed rewrite test; its null concerns local class assignment, not every operator or lexical mechanism.
precise_completion_conditions: Name one directed surface rewrite or a finite separately motivated context-conditioned rule; fix direction and conditioning before outcome inspection.
Declare preserved raw unit and projection/error assumptions. Select one observable physical or written-role endpoint and explain differing predictions under a specified rival.
Identify actual additional independent instances and a held unit for that frozen rule; verify capacity before fitting. Known meanings are not required for a structural endpoint.
outcome_changes_if_defined: Counterexamples can reject a restricted unconditional rewrite-to-class rule; transferred predicted structural behavior could support that rule over a genuinely distinct rival. Neither outcome alone chooses a meaning. Presently even this smallest rule is not fixed, so no manuscript test is selected.
